scope: grouped-gemm big-group fix attempt + worker truncation discovery + PLE table over one-sided RDMA

corruption_found.what: the worker (tools/cold_expert_worker.cpp) built NATURAL groups (one per expert) and the grouped kernel served at most GMAX=8 entries per group, silently TRUNCATING the rest; a 2048-token window routes ~57 entries/expert, so ~86% of remote rows at 4K chunk-2048 were stale scratch
corruption_found.consequence: round-151's 545.84 tok/s @4K was computed with garbage remote rows - its speed was partly skipped work. Honest full-compute baseline after the fix: 497.4 tok/s
corruption_found.proof: Spark standalone (independent f16 path) real_prompt4096 first-16 tokens = 1118 3817 318 14472 3860 8 248046 198 248045 74455 198 248068 198 760 1156 682 - matches the FIXED cross-machine run, differs from round-151's corrupted output at token 6
corruption_found.fix: worker host-side sub-grouping into <=8-entry runs (WGMAX), matching the kernel's contract

kernel_experiments.tile_loop_register_resident_weights: 4859ms gather @4K - SLOWER than host-split (3652ms); register preload cut occupancy, longer per-block serial chains
kernel_experiments.lane_per_entry_big_kernel: 21121ms gather @4K - catastrophic; 34B scattered global activation reads waste 8x L2 bandwidth; kernels kept in tree but only reached by device-side dispatch for ne>8 (MTP/verify safety net, previously silently truncated there too)
kernel_experiments.conclusion: the grouped kernel is latency/occupancy-bound, NOT weight-bandwidth-bound (re-reads were ~7% of gather); many small independent blocks win. True engine-side hit-kernel cost is ~700ms of the 4K wall (0.62us/row); the gather segment was mostly PEER WAIT all along

ple_over_rdma.design: worker --ple-gguf loads the 28.8GB IQ4_NL table into pinned RAM, expose_region(REMOTE_READ), publishes PleInfo (addr/rkey/rows) in ring slot 0 before serving; engine fetch_ple_info polls slot 0 after tier open, PleReader remote backend serves the row cache then one-sided chained reads (48 rows per WR chain, QP max_send_wr=64) via new RemoteStage::rdma_read_rows; --ple-io rdma, fail-closed
ple_over_rdma.infra: Spark needed /etc/security/limits.d/<spark>-memlock.conf (memlock unlimited) for the 28.8GB registration - done
ple_over_rdma.numerics: 512 and 4K outputs bit-identical to the Spark standalone ground truth

verdict: 520.3 vs 1226 = 42% - BELOW baseline; the wall is now the worker: 836K remote rows, ~40ms service per 2048-token window (transfer ~110MB f32 results + 21MB activations, then GB10 compute)
next_levers_ranked: 1. shrink window transfer: results f32->fp16 (89->44.5MB/window) and activations f32->q8_0 (engine already quantizes pf_q8; 21->5.4MB) - worth ~1.5-2s of the 4.4s peer wait; gate on token match vs ground truth
2. profile.bin regeneration from real routing traces (prefill hit 55% -> decode-level 90% halves remote rows AND transfer)
3. worker kernel throughput on GB10 (latency-bound tile kernel; bigger GMAX with dynamic shared on sm_121, or row-parallel redesign)
